source: Original (freshly authored 2026-10-07, calculator allowed); parallel of 1-9PQ_Sequences P1(a)-(d). Arithmetic sequence 15, 23, 31, 39, ...; d = 8; u_n = 15 + 8(n - 1); u_30 = 247; 303 is u_37.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down the common difference d of the arithmetic sequence 15, 23, 31, 39, ...

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find an expression for u_n, the nth term.
parts.tolerance: Accept any equivalent expression, e.g. 8n + 7; the substituted form is preferred but not required.
parts.notes: (M1) for the arithmetic nth-term formula with u_1 = 15 and d = 8, implied by a correct answer. A1 for a correct expression. u_n = 15 + 8n earns M1A0.
parts.follow_through: Uses d from part (a); award A1 for a correct expression from the student's own d.

parts.label: c
parts.notes: (M1) for substituting n = 30 into the nth-term formula, e.g. 15 + 8(30 - 1). A1 for 247. 15 + 8(30) = 255 (u_31) earns M0A0.
parts.follow_through: Uses the expression from part (b); award A1 for the correct value from the student's own expression.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Show that 303 is a term of the sequence, and find which term it is.
parts.tolerance: Accept 8n + 7 = 303 giving n = 37, or a table search showing u_37 = 303.
parts.notes: M1 for setting the nth-term expression equal to 303. A1 for n = 37. R1 for the conclusion that 303 is a term because n is a positive whole number; a bare 'n = 37' earns M1A1R0.
parts.follow_through: Uses the expression from part (b); award R1 for a conclusion correctly drawn from the student's own n.

source: Original (freshly authored 2026-10-07, calculator allowed); parallel of 1-9PQ_Sequences P2(a), (c), (d). Arithmetic sequence with u_5 = 38, u_14 = 11: d = -3, u_1 = 50; first negative term u_18 = -1. Second sequence 2k + 1, 4k - 3, 5k + 1: k = 8, terms 17, 29, 41.

parts.label: a
parts.description: In an arithmetic sequence u_5 = 38 and u_14 = 11. Find d and u_1.
parts.notes: M1 for any valid method relating the two terms (both equations u_1 + 4d = 38 and u_1 + 13d = 11, d = (u_14 - u_5)/(14 - 5), or GDC system). A1 for d = -3, A1 for u_1 = 50, independent.
parts.follow_through: Award the second A1 for u_1 correct from the student's own d.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the first term of the sequence that is negative.
parts.tolerance: Accept an equation in place of the inequality, or a table search showing u_17 = 2 and u_18 = -1; a single row u_18 = -1 still earns full marks with a feedback note.
parts.notes: M1 for an inequality, equation or table using the nth-term expression. A1 for n = 18 (from n > 17.67). A1 for the term -1. A final answer of 'n = 18' alone earns M1A1A0: the question asks for the term.
parts.follow_through: Uses u_1 and d from part (a); award marks for values correctly found from the student's own u_1 and d.

parts.label: c
parts.description: The first three terms of an arithmetic sequence are 2k + 1, 4k - 3, 5k + 1. Find k and write down the first three terms.
parts.notes: M1 for equating the two differences. A1 for k = 8. A1 for the terms 17, 29, 41.
parts.follow_through: Award the final A1 for three terms correctly evaluated from the student's own k.

source: Original (freshly authored 2026-10-07, calculator allowed); parallel of 1-9PQ_Sequences P3(a), (b), (d), (f). Classify 5,10,20,40 (geometric r = 2); 7,4,1,-2 (arithmetic d = -3); 2,3,5,8 (neither); 162,54,18,6 (geometric r = 1/3). Geometric 16, 20, 25, ...: r = 1.25, u_12 = 16(1.25)^11 = 186.26. Challenge: u_3 = 45, u_6 = 1215 gives r = 3, u_1 = 5.

parts.label: a
parts.description: State whether each sequence is arithmetic, geometric or neither, with d or r: (i) 5, 10, 20, 40 (ii) 7, 4, 1, -2 (iii) 2, 3, 5, 8 (iv) 162, 54, 18, 6.
parts.notes: A1 for each sequence: the type and, for (i), (ii) and (iv), the correct d or r. d = 3 in (ii) earns A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the common ratio r of the geometric sequence 16, 20, 25, ...

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find u_12 of the geometric sequence 16, 20, 25, ...
parts.follow_through: Uses r from part (b); award A1 for the correct value from the student's own r.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Challenge: a geometric sequence has u_3 = 45 and u_6 = 1215. Find the common ratio and the first term.
parts.notes: M1 for r^3 = 1215/45 = 27 (or the two equations u_1 r^2 = 45, u_1 r^5 = 1215 divided). A1 for r = 3. A1 for u_1 = 5. u_1 = 45/3 = 15 earns M1A1A0.
parts.follow_through: Award the final A1 for u_1 correct from the student's own r.

source: Original (freshly authored 2026-10-07, calculator allowed); parallel of 1-9PQ_Sequences P4(a)-(c), with (a) and (b) swapped. Job A: 38000 rising by 2000 per year (arithmetic). Job B: 36000 rising by 6% per year (geometric). Year 3: A 42000, B 40449.60. B first exceeds A in year 6 (A 48000, B 48176.12; year 5: A 46000, B 45449.17).

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down an expression for the salary in year n for each job (Job A: $38000 rising by $2000 each year; Job B: $36000 rising by 6% each year).
parts.tolerance: Accept any equivalent expression, e.g. A_n = 36000 + 2000n.
parts.notes: A1 for A_n. A1 for B_n. r = 0.06 or r = 6, or exponent n instead of n - 1, earns A0 for B_n.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the salary in year 3 for each job.
parts.tolerance: Accept 40400 (3 s.f.) or 40450 for Job B.
parts.follow_through: Award each A1 for the value from the student's own expression in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the first year in which the Job B salary is greater than the Job A salary.
parts.tolerance: Accept a GDC table, a graph, or solving the equation on the GDC (n = 5.78...). A single row (B_6 > A_6) still earns full marks with a feedback note that year 5 justifies 'first'.
parts.notes: (M1) for a valid comparison of the two expressions. A1 for the two adjacent years (or n = 5.78). A1 for year 6. 'Year 5.78' as the final answer earns M1A1A0.
parts.follow_through: Uses the expressions from part (a); award marks for a comparison correctly made from the student's own expressions.
